scope: Static source-runtime reconciliation only; no WordPress or browser mutation.

disproved_previous_interpretation.stale_claim: By-user prev/next/dot/Arrow/swipe navigation sets manual=true, permanently latching autoplay off.
disproved_previous_interpretation.direct_source_code_finding: FALSE. The local variable manual is initialized once from c.classList.contains('carousel--manual') and is never assigned afterward. go(n) has no by-user argument. Successful manual navigation paths call go(...) followed by start().
disproved_previous_interpretation.risk_if_uncorrected: A source-correct target that restarts autoplay after manual navigation could be misclassified as a failure and receive an unnecessary/regressive runtime change.

correct_contract: manual is a static per-instance class-derived flag: true only when the carousel root has carousel--manual at initialization.
start() always clears the existing timer first; it creates a new 4000ms interval only when manual is false, reduced-motion is false, slides>=2 and the root remains connected.

Prev/next arrow click, dot click, ArrowLeft/ArrowRight and qualifying pointer swipe all call start() after moving. On a non-manual carousel this resets/restarts the autoplay interval; it does not permanently stop autoplay.

mouseenter and focusin stop(); mouseleave and focusout call start() without independent pause flags, so compound hover/focus exit ordering can restart autoplay while the other condition is still active. This surprising behavior is source contract until live reference disproves the recovered runtime.
A prefers-reduced-motion change calls start(). Turning reduce off restarts autoplay on a connected non-manual multi-slide instance; turning it on suppresses the new interval.
Broken-slide removal reindexes dots and may stop/hide the carousel based on remaining slide count.

Compound hover+focus and reduced-motion behavior must be compared as observable source parity, not redesigned to an ideal policy.
